name: EthOS VM Manager
description: Run Windows and Linux virtual machines on this NAS with hardware acceleration. Create a VM from an ISO, boot it, and use it from the browser console - no separate computer left running. Disks live on your own shares, VMs start again after a restart, and every VM is isolated in its own process.
author: SyncHot
changelog: 1.0.5: the window shows a calm “Starting engine…” state while the first-run QEMU/noVNC installation is still running, instead of a connection-reset error. 1.0.4: the console no longer reserves host port 8094 — Docker maps the container port to a free host port and the window discovers it, so the package starts even when another service already uses 8094. 1.0.3: requires EthOS 2.0. 1.0.2: the console overlay no longer covers the window — it is hidden until you press Console, so the machine list and the create form are always visible. 1.0.1: the browser console connects again — the WebSocket handshake now selects the `binary` subprotocol noVNC asks for, which browsers otherwise reject. Port 8094 shows a short explanation instead of raw JSON when opened directly, the create form pre-fills a real storage root, and picking a folder fills the ISO list automatically. 1.0.0: first release. KVM virtual machines with a browser console: create a VM from an ISO stored on the NAS, start, stop and reset it, follow its live status, and let it start automatically with EthOS. Disks are qcow2 files on a share you pick. Snapshots, cloning and OVA export follow in 1.1.
